$comment_cao: The CAO LANE: interactive, hierarchical, multi-provider orchestration through
the CAO server. The PowerShell batch runner ignores this block entirely; the
Python lane (cao/) reads ONLY this block. One file, two lanes.
maxDepth is REAL, not advisory. cao/profiles.py generates one profile per
level and emits the deepest one WITHOUT assign/handoff, so it cannot spawn --
the tool is absent from the terminal. This matters most for Gemini: `agy` has
no --no-subagents flag (claude and grok do), so withholding the tool is the
only leaf control that actually holds. Raise maxDepth and regenerate; never
hand-edit a generated profile.
worktreeRoot must sit on a NATIVE filesystem. Measured on a Windows host:
`git status` costs 3.021s against /mnt/c (9p) versus 0.146s in an ext4
worktree whose .git still lives on /mnt/c -- a 20x difference paid on every
file operation of a long-horizon run. On Linux this is already native.
routing maps a task CLASS to an ORDERED ladder. The dispatcher takes the first
candidate whose pool is open, so a ladder is simultaneously a preference order
and a quota fallback -- there is no second structure for the two to disagree.
pool vs family: pool = which quota bucket pays; family = whose blind spots.
They differ. claude-opus-4-6-thinking via agy is the anthropic FAMILY from the
antigravity POOL: good extra capacity, and an invalid reviewer for
Claude-written code. NEVER decline a pool because its best model is older than
another pool's -- that shrinks the budget without improving the model.

$comment_levels: Each level carries its own pool/model, so the hierarchy is genuinely mixed:
judgement at the top, cheap execution below. A Claude supervisor reviewing a
DeepSeek worker is ALREADY cross-family, so review costs no extra dispatch.
A leaf SHOULD sit on a hard-enforcement provider (claude_code, opencode_cli,
grok_cli, kiro_cli, copilot_cli). On antigravity_cli, CAO documents tool
restrictions as advisory, so a leaf there is policed only by cao/monitor.py.
